articles.title: MAGA Republican Flees Own Presser When Cornered on Son-in-Law’s Nazi Posts
articles.description: Nathan Howard / REUTERS Republican Senate candidate Mike Collins’ press conference abruptly ended after reporters questioned him about his son-in-law’s pro-Nazi online posts. Rep. Collins, who has been a congressman in a reliably red Georgia district since 2023, on Thursday tried to shift the topic to his Democratic opponent, Sen. Jon Ossoff. But reporters pressed the issue, and Collins ultimately walked away from the podium with minimal comments about how David Alan Scheer II, according to a CNN investigation, is “a pro-White nationalist and social media influencer with a track record of sharing antisemitic material and Nazi imagery in comments across the internet.” Towards the end of Collins’ seven-minute press conference outside the Monroe County Hospital, a reporter asked him if he wanted to comment on what Scheer posted online, like how, “There’s nothing wrong with White Nationalism.” Scheer also shared Nazi imagery. Read more at The Daily Beast.

articles.title: World: Victims of Trafficking in Human Beings in Asylum and Reception (Situational Update Issue No 26, 30 July 2026)
articles.description: Country: World Source: European Union Agency for Asylum Please refer to the attached file. The information presented in this Situational Update complements the developments reported in the Asylum Report 2026. It is a follow-up to Fact Sheet No 34, covering the period 1 July 2025-30 June 2026. EU legislation contains provisions which address asylum applicants with special needs who may be considered particularly vulnerable, including victims of human trafficking. These provisions ensure that vulnerable applicants receive adequate support to benefit from their rights and comply with the obligations, which are defined under the Common European Asylum System (CEAS). EU Member States were obligated to transpose the revised EU Anti-Trafficking Directive by 15 July 2026, which aims to address emerging challenges and strengthen strategic and operational responses to tackling human trafficking. One of the main requirements is to adopt a national action plan by 2028 to ensure a coordinated and sustainable response to human trafficking and establish formal referral mechanisms and national focal points for cross-border referral of victims In parallel, the entry into force of the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum in June 2026 fostered the development of tools to strengthen early identification of vulnerable persons, including presumed trafficking victims, in asylum and reception systems and to have an effective national referral system.

articles.title: I’ve seen what can confound Farage on his home turf: optimism. People need a politics that offers them that | Owen Jones
articles.description: You can’t blame his constituents in Clacton for their pessimism – because they have been let down for years Under battered England flags, cynicism, pessimism and exhaustion stalk the streets of Clacton. As the byelection called by Nigel Farage approaches, one young couple do not know which candidates are standing. Neither has ever voted. Living in Britain is “depressing”, says the woman in a black floral dress. “The cost of living these days is stupid,” says her partner, wearing a black and grey mechanic’s shirt and a black and red cap. They both work 40 or 50 hours a week, he says, yet “we’re still struggling to pay rent, food, electric, everything else”. They rarely get a day off, and time spent together is rarer still.
